message.content: Work GitHub issue #64 in this repo using the /hq-work workflow (read AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md). Claim with `./hq claim 64 --agent claude`, build strictly inside the issue's Scope, run `bun install` in the worktree first, run `./hq check`, rebase on origin/main, open the PR with `./hq pr 64 --body-file .context/pr-64.md` (add --allow-dirty only for untracked generated files you deliberately did not commit; retry once if the push is rejected with commit_refs_rules), then stop and report PR number and evidence. Do not ship/merge. Run the anti-slop skill on changed UI. Device-only and keyed steps are left for a human. Never read .env files. A local test `speak > names a missing api key from a fresh process` may fail only because of a git-ignored .env.local; say so rather than working around it.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: hq-work
3	description: 'Use when a human assigns you a GitHub issue ("work on #N" or "/hq-work N"). Takes it from claim to a reviewed PR.'
4	---
5	
6	# hq-work
7	
8	`N` = issue, `<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`, `<PR>` = PR number. Windows: `hq.cmd` for `./hq`.
9	
10	1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`. If it refuses, stop and tell the human why. Read what it
11	   prints: the issue, work in flight, overlapping files.
12	2. Context before code. Read only the docs the issue needs, then run
13	   `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"` and `entire brain brief "<task>"`.
14	   Before rewriting code you did not write: `entire why <file>:<line>`.
15	3. Plan inline in a few bullets. No spec or plan documents.
16	4. Build inside Scope, never in "Do not touch". Small commits, staged by name:
17	   `git add <file> <file> && git commit -m "<what the product can now do>"`.
18	   Push whenever you like: `git push -u origin HEAD`.
19	5. Verify: run the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check` until it passes.
20	6. Sync with main. Not pushed yet: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`. Already pushed:
21	   `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (never force-push). Fix conflicts in your own
22	   changes, `git add <files>`, then `git rebase --continue` or `git commit`. Re-run `./hq check`.
23	7. Write `.context/pr-N.md` (template below; `mkdir -p .context` if needed), then
24	   `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`. It pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N` and sets
25	   `status:review`. Get the number: `gh pr view --json number,url`.
26	8. Trail: Entire opens a trail for your PR by itself. Check it with `entire trail show`, then run `entire trail ci-pr` (safe to re-run). Only if `trail show` finds none: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`.
27	9. Review, unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`. Fix real findings, commit, `git push`,
28	   re-run `./hq check`. Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
29	10. Report the PR link, check result and risks, then stop. Merge only on "ship it" (`/hq-ship`).
30	
31	PR body template for `.context/pr-N.md`:
32	
33	````markdown
34	## What changed
35	- <what the product can now do>
36	
37	## How verified
38	- <Verify steps you ran and what you saw>
39	```
40	<tail of ./hq check>
41	```
42	
43	## Risks
44	- <what could break, or "none">
45	
46	## Screenshots
47	<UI changes only, else "n/a">
48	````
49	
50	Out of scope: do not do it. Write `.context/new-issue.md` with the headings `### Goal`,
51	`### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`,
52	`### Notes` (say "Found while working on #N" in Notes), then
53	`gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/new-issue.md --label status:needs-human`.
54	Link it on your issue: `gh issue comment N --body "Follow-up: #M"`. Carry on with your own scope.
55	
56	Stuck (unclear criteria, waiting on another issue, a conflict in code you did not write):
57	`./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.
58	
59	Done means: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open
60	with evidence, `review:pass` (unless `size:S`).

### Goal

Demo step 5: switch from light sleeper to night out and watch the ranking change.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Show a four-profile picker, stay dates, a ranked list and Mapbox hotel score markers from the same `stays.rank` result.
- [ ] Selecting a hotel in the list selects and focuses its map marker, and selecting a marker focuses the matching list row and breakdown.
- [ ] Changing profile or stay dates updates scores, order and marker styling together; no stale selection is left pointing at another hotel.
- [ ] Each hotel opens a per-input breakdown with its source IDs one tap away and the label "estimate"; do not imply a room-level score.
- [ ] The works penalty is visible only for overlapping stay dates; placeholder booking links and simulated cohort inputs are labelled.
- [ ] An unavailable API falls back to the shared fixture with an explicit sample/simulated-data label; web and iOS behave equivalently.

### Scope

- `apps/mobile/src/features/stays/`

33:### Rules for the score
34-- It is an estimate and the UI says so. Every score has its sources one tap away: which sensors,
35-  which permits, how many real nights. Without this, low-scoring hotels will dispute it.
36-- Weights live in one place, `packages/shared/src/domain/`, so the app can show the breakdown.
37-- Simulated cohort nights are flagged and labelled wherever they affect a score.
38-
39-## Revenue
40-1. **Affiliate commission (launch).** Booking links through affiliate networks. Booking.com cut
41-   thousands of smaller affiliates in 2025 and moved them to networks such as Awin and CJ;
42-   Expedia Group's affiliate programme and aggregators such as Travelpayouts are the other routes
43-   for a small team. Affiliate approval takes weeks, so the demo uses OpenStreetMap hotels with
44-   placeholder booking links. Don't quote a commission rate until it's confirmed.
45-2. **Verified Quiet (year one).** Hotels that already score well pay a yearly fee to replace the
46-   estimate with measured, room-by-room data from in-room sensors. Hotels that score badly get a
47-   free report showing which rooms and hours are the problem, as the route to a better score.
48-3. **Data licensing (later).** Area-level sleep disturbance data for councils, developers
49-   scheduling construction, and estate agents.
50-
51-## Hypotheses, not findings
52-- Renters choosing a flat for a 12-month lease may be a bigger market than hotel guests: same
53-  score, higher stakes. Pitch it as the next market, not as evidence.
54-
55-## Judge questions
56-| Question | Answer |
57-|---|---|
58-| Is this real data? | The city map, the recorded night and the permits are real; other users are simulated and labelled on the map |

content.thinking:
The fixture only has two profiles and no permits, so I'm looking at what I can compute client-side. For bestValue, I could reweight the fixture's component values with the same weights as lightSleeper plus a price factor, but the station value isn't in the payload, so the business fallback is harder. The simplest honest option seems to be a fallback just for bestValue.

I'm weighing whether to rescore the fixture's profiles client-side with the same weights, with the business case needing a note since the station value is missing from the sample.

I'm checking whether the light-sleeper fixture has any nightlife values, and I'm deciding how to show the works penalty: only when a permit actually overlaps the stay dates, with the roadworks row handled separately.

I'm settling the stay-date controls: instead of typing dates, I'll use steppers for check-in day and number of nights, defaulting to the fixture's 20–22 November so the demo is deterministic. I'm also checking whether the mock layer will supply the permit data I need.

I'm settling on map markers colored in three ink-grey shades by score band, with the selected marker outlined, and I'll include the score in each feature's properties. Markers stay unclustered.

Checking how the map's center prop reacts to changes, and whether the stays query falls back to the fixture while a new input is still loading.

I'm deciding how to handle the stay-date picker and the loading state: if the profile changes, the old results shouldn't stick around, so I'll show a loading state and drop the selection whenever the chosen hotel isn't in the new result set. I also still need to check how the map handles changes to its center prop and whether the light-sleeper sample has any nightlife values.

I'm checking whether the `test` script in the packages and apps/server covers mobile tests, since `./hq check` might include them and `city.test.ts` exists. The fixture dates are fixed to November 20 through 22, so for other dates I'd relabel them to the chosen ones while keeping the scores. The fallback will reweight from the lightSleeper fixture for bestValue and business.

I'm settling on a simple fallback module: sample ranks will use the nightOut fixture directly, and for bestValue and business I'll rescore from the lightSleeper fixture with price weighting and with the station distance weight dropped, renormalising over the remaining five inputs and noting that in the sample.

I'm working out the model layer next: the profile labels, date helpers for check-in and nights, the sample fallback, the breakdown rows, and the penalty visibility. After that comes the selection logic, which keeps a stale hotel id from being re-selected when the list reloads.

I'm working out how the map markers and the breakdown rows should look. The selection will stay on the same hotel id across profile changes, and the map will center on the selected hotel at zoom 14, falling back to Newcastle at zoom 13, with the center value memoized so the effect doesn't re-run. Each breakdown row will show the label, value, weight percentage, and points, with the sensor and permit sources listed underneath.

I'm working out the works penalty next. It's the roadworks weight times how far the roadworks score falls short of 100, and it only appears when a permit overlaps the stay, with the count of overlapping permits shown alongside. The booking link will open through Linking and sit on a button.

I'm setting up the booking link as a secondary button captioned as a placeholder, not a real booking, and a note that each hotel is an estimate of its surrounding area rather than a specific room. Rows will show rank, name, score and price, expanding on tap, with the list in a scroll view beneath the map. When a marker is selected, I'll scroll to that row using stored layout positions.

I'm wiring up the map effect on the selected hotel and getting the rows in order, then I'll write the files.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/nick/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/tripoli/.claude/skills/anti-slop

If `.ux-profile.md` exists at the project root, read it before changing layout, color, or type.

### Intent

AI-generated and template-driven UI converges on the same clichés: rainbow buttons, frosted glass panels, cartoon empty states, and decorative chrome that adds no function. This skill bans those patterns so interfaces stay purposeful, readable, and aligned with the rest of the visual-taste skills.

### Hard Rules (Non-Negotiable)

- **No multi-color radial rainbow gradients on standard CTA buttons.** Primary actions use a solid fill or a single-hue subtle gradient (same hue, ≤10% lightness shift). Ban `conic-gradient`, multi-stop rainbow `linear-gradient`, and purple-to-orange radial fills on default buttons.
- **No glassmorphic blur (`backdrop-filter`) without high-contrast boundary.** If blur is used at all, the panel must have a visible 1px border ≥3:1 against whatever shows through, opaque fallback when `backdrop-filter` unsupported, and sufficient text contrast. Default product UI should omit blur entirely.
- **No generic cartoon vector people** (waving, high-fiving, empty-box mascots) in empty states. Use text, actionable CTAs, simple monochrome icons, or product-relevant screenshots — not stock illustration people.
- **No icons inside inputs unless functional.** Allowed: search magnifier, clear/reset control, password visibility toggle. Banned: decorative leading icons on every text field, emoji-style adorners, brand icons inside standard inputs.
- **No unnecessary pill containers around standard text metadata.** Timestamps, author names, file sizes, and tags render as plain text or minimal chips only when they are interactive filters. Do not wrap static metadata in rounded pastel pills for decoration.
- **Anti-slop deletes decoration, not structure.** Remove pills, glass, cartoons, and decorative chrome. Do **not** delete the list frame, row dividers, or search chrome. An empty-looking table after a slop pass is a **fail**, not a pass.

### Design Heuristics & Taste Principles

- When a element's only job is decoration, delete it.
- Prefer one neutral border and whitespace over gradients, blobs, and floating shapes.
- Empty states sell the next action, not illustration budget.
- If it appears in a generic SaaS landing template, assume it is slop until proven functional.
- Cross-check `.ux-profile.md` banned list — it may extend these rules.

### Concrete Scenarios (Before vs. After)

#### ❌ Anti-Pattern

Sign-up uses a `conic-gradient` "Get Started" button. Login form inputs each have a leading gray icon. Empty project view shows a cartoon character high-fiving. Settings show "Last updated" inside a lavender pill. A modal uses `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)` with no border on a busy background.

#### ✅ Best Practice

Primary CTA is solid accent fill. Search field keeps one magnifier icon; other fields are label + input only. Empty state: heading, one sentence of value, "Create project" button, optional simple 24px monochrome icon. Metadata runs as 12px secondary text. Modal uses opaque L3 surface, 1px border, optional scrim — no blur.

### Framework-Agnostic Implementation Blueprint

**Audit pass (grep / search changed files):**

```
backdrop-filter
conic-gradient
linear-gradient.*(#.*,#.*,#)   /* multi-hue gradients on buttons */
illustration|empty-state.*svg  /* review for cartoon people */
border-radius: 999             /* pill wrappers on static text */
```

**Replace patterns:**

```css
/* ❌ Slop */
.btn-primary {
  background: conic-gradient(from 180deg, #f00, #ff0, #0f0, #00f, #f0f);
}
.panel {
  backdrop-filter: blur(16px);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
}

/* ✅ Restrained */
.btn-primary {
  background: var(--accent);
}
.panel {
  background: var(--surface-l3);
  border: 1px solid var(--border-l2);
}
```

Use [reference/slop-checklist.md](reference/slop-checklist.md) for the full identification matrix.

### Agent Checklist

- [ ] Read `.ux-profile.md` if present; merge its ban list with this skill.
- [ ] Scan CTAs — no rainbow or multi-hue radial gradients.
- [ ] Scan overlays — no unbounded glassmorphism; border + opaque fallback if blur exists.
- [ ] Scan empty states — no cartoon people illustrations.
- [ ] Scan inputs — icons only where functional (search, clear, toggle).
- [ ] Scan metadata — no decorative pill wrappers on static text.
- [ ] After a slop pass: list frame, row dividers, and search chrome still present — an empty-looking table is a fail.
- [ ] Run slop checklist matrix on any AI-generated or imported component.
